behaviors.title: Routine updates preserve persistent service registration
invariants: An unchanged loaded LaunchAgent is restarted without being booted out or bootstrapped again.
A missing or materially changed LaunchAgent takes an explicit registration path.

scenarios.title: LaunchAgent updates distinguish restart from registration
scenarios.oracle: Lifecycle tests prove missing services bootstrap, unchanged loaded services only kickstart, changed loaded services re-register, and ordinary app promotion contains no bootout or bootstrap path for the loaded collector.

behaviors.title: Behavior audit exposes repository gaps and gates automation
invariants: A selected repository with a Tier-0 assurance gap never produces a ready audit.
Fleet filters change selection without changing the underlying assurance state.

scenarios.title: Missing assurance is machine-readable and non-zero
scenarios.oracle: pronto behavior --json reports selected repositories and gaps and exits non-zero whenever any selected repository is not release-ready.

scenarios.title: Fleet gaps can be selected without synthesized compliance
scenarios.oracle: The behavior command filters missing, legacy, unprofiled, stale, failed, and blocked repositories while preserving each repository's exact projected state.

behaviors.title: Quality Runner evidence remains conservative through projection
invariants: Target mismatch removes both release readiness and current edge-verification claims.
Profile, freshness, result, and release status remain separate dimensions.

scenarios.title: Missing, invalid, or stale evidence never becomes verified
scenarios.oracle: Missing, invalid, stale, failed, blocked, and target-mismatched evidence projects as not release-ready; only current passing Tier-0 evidence or an explicit valid not-applicable contract is release-ready.

behaviors.title: Release readiness requires behavior assurance
invariants: Tier 1 and Tier 2 edge gaps never silently widen the Tier-0 release gate.

scenarios.title: Release preview blocks on assurance gaps
scenarios.oracle: Release preparation is blocked and explains the Tier-0 behavior-assurance state unless the repository projection is release-ready.

behaviors.title: Portfolio users can inspect release and edge assurance separately
invariants: The installed app never presents whole-inventory edge coverage as release readiness.
Security-sensitive traces expose categories and hashes without raw payloads.

scenarios.title: Quality workspace distinguishes release and edge durability
scenarios.oracle: The Quality workspace visibly separates Tier-0 release assurance from all-tier verified and profiled counts, freshness, failed, blocked, and unknown states, and fleet filters.

behaviors.title: Pronto exposes live custody evidence without granting mutation authority
invariants: Custody state comes from live Git and local receipts rather than cached Pronto labels.
Lifecycle state is separate from granular disposition and next action; unknown is never the only explanation.
Unsupported, malformed, legacy unsigned, binding-mismatched, dirty, active-operation, and unavailable-evidence lanes remain preserved and are never projected as adoptable.
The CLI and renderer show the projection as read-only and never imply permission to adopt, integrate, delete, or push.

scenarios.title: Custody CLI exposes machine-readable live evidence
scenarios.oracle: pronto custody --json emits pronto-custody-cli/v1 with lane states, disposition_counts, next_safe_step, read_only=true, and implementation_allowed=false; a synthetic unleased worktree is surfaced without changing Git state.

scenarios.title: Evidence gaps remain actionable rather than catch-all unknown
scenarios.oracle: Malformed, unsupported-schema, legacy-unsigned, binding-mismatch, dirty, operation-active, and unavailable-evidence fixtures retain distinct dispositions, next actions, and non-adoptable states.

scenarios.title: Repository detail shows custody state and reason
scenarios.oracle: The repository detail surface displays custody lifecycle counts and each lane's granular disposition and next action without offering mutation controls.
